chunk_findings.detail: The diff moves the `find_spec` import from old line 88 to module level, but the reported failing guard also flagged a deferred import at `services/embed.py:46`. That line is not touched by this diff, so `tests/test_architecture_guards.py::test_ratchet[deferred_imports]` will still report it and fail. The change therefore does not close the reported bug for the second deferred import in this file.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_git_merge` is deterministic and uses only the two source trees for conflict detection; both destinations in the test, `tmp_path / "m"` and `tmp_path / "m2"`, start absent and the sources `c1`/`c2` are unchanged between the calls. Therefore the first call at line 117 and the second call at line 127 must behave identically with respect to `FileExistsError`. If the second call raises, the first call must have already raised before the assertions and escaped the test; if the second call does not raise, `pytest.raises(FileExistsError)` fails. No execution passes this test as changed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_hot_cold_design_fixture.py:127 (and `_git_merge` at :19)

chunk_findings.detail: The new call `CV.upgrade_advice(highest, install_kind())` resolves `install_kind` from `_skew`'s own module scope, not from the public `ddflow.infra.log` package attribute. The removed deferred import existed so that callers/tests monkeypatching `ddflow.infra.log.install_kind` would be honored. A concrete failure: `monkeypatch.setattr(LOG, "install_kind", lambda: "source-tree")` followed by `LOG.skew_message("0.1.0", "0.2.0", "bob")` will now ignore that patch and use `_skew.install_kind`'s real detection, producing the wrong remedy. The two updated tests only patch `LOG._skew` instead, so they hide this regression for those tests but leave any caller still using the previously supported `LOG.install_kind` injection point broken.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: when the recorded worktree path no longer exists, `tree.is_dir()` is false and `_tree_let_go` returns `False`. Therefore `_worktree_held_by` still treats an open, released+merged item with no directory on disk as holding the tree. Input: item A is open, `lease is None`, `merged_sha` is set, `worktree == stored`, but the directory was removed; `_worktree_held_by` returns A and a new claim for the same `stored` path is refused. The triage’s “not introduced here” does not answer this: the code remains byte-identical in the move, so the behavior persists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_tree.py:_tree_let_go

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: the detached/ancestor check `W.git(path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", f"refs/heads/{branch}", "HEAD").ok` is normally false during an actual rebase or conflict, because the branch ref still points at the original tip while HEAD is detached at a new/cherry-picked commit. For an item whose worktree is mid-rebase, `_recorded_tree` returns `None`, so a re-claim does not bind to the item’s own existing tree. The triage’s “not introduced here” does not answer this; the moved body is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_tree.py:_is_items_tree

chunk_findings.detail: The new fallback is still false for a rebase of a different branch when the item branch is an ancestor of the detached HEAD. `W.git(path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ref, "HEAD").ok` is evaluated first, and if it is true the `or` short-circuits before `_rebasing(path) == ref` is checked. Concrete input: `main` is at C, `feature` is at C-D-E, and the worktree is stopped in `git rebase main feature` with `head-name=refs/heads/feature`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor refs/heads/main HEAD` succeeds, so `_is_items_tree(path, "main")` returns `True`. The path is therefore claimed as `main`'s tree even though it is rebasing `feature`, which is exactly what `test_a_tree_rebasing_another_branch_is_not_the_items_tree` should reject. The existing worktree is mis-identified and a claim for `main` can bind to another branch's in-progress rebase.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_tree.py:_is_items_tree

chunk_findings.detail: This change does not fix the bug it is stated to fix. It only modifies `ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim_tree.py` and `tests/test_lease_tree_identity.py`; nothing splits or otherwise reduces `ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py`. The deterministic reproduction remains: `uv run pytest -q tests/test_lifecycle_layout.py` still fails because `ddflow.api.lifecycle.claim is 612 lines; assert 612 < 600`. So the red monolith ratchet for `claim.py` is untouched.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test executes `subprocess.run(["git", "rebase", "main"], cwd=tree, ...)` directly, bypassing the project git port required by [r-adapters]. Every other git invocation in this file is routed through the `_git` helper, so this one raw subprocess makes the regression test depend on host git behavior and avoids the adapter/fake boundary the rule exists to enforce.
